title: The control block
body: struct spsc_ring: the buffer of int (read-only after creation), the capacity and its mask, then the consumer's head and the producer's tail, each _Atomic uint64_t aligned on its own cache line, the separation proven by a _Static_assert.
rationale: One place holds every field both sides read; the layout decides the false sharing.

title: Creation and teardown
body: spsc_ring_init(): the capacity checked, the control block from aligned_alloc at its alignment, the counters initialised, the lock-free probe of both counters, then the buffer from calloc; spsc_ring_destroy() frees both and clears the caller's pointer; spsc_ring_reset() stores 0 in both counters.
rationale: Creation refuses before it allocates the buffer; every failure frees what was taken.

title: The producer side
body: spsc_ring_push() and spsc_ring_is_full(): the tail read relaxed (the producer owns it), the head read with acquire, the slot written, the tail advanced with release.
rationale: Only the producer writes the tail and the slots it fills.

title: The consumer side
body: spsc_ring_pop() and spsc_ring_is_empty(): the head read relaxed (the consumer owns it), the tail read with acquire, the slot read, the head advanced with release.
rationale: Only the consumer writes the head.

title: The queries
body: spsc_ring_capacity() returns the fixed size; spsc_ring_size() reads the head then the tail, both with acquire, and clamps the difference to the capacity.
rationale: The head read first can never exceed the tail read after it.

title: The test seams (tests only)
body: Under SPSC_RING_TESTING only: the allocators replaced through tests/UTs/spscring_test_hooks.h and the lock-free verdict of each counter overridden, so that the unit suite reaches every failure path; without the switch the allocators are the C library's macros and nothing is exported.
rationale: Every branch of creation is covered without hoping malloc fails.
